missed.why: P2 did not consider the TCAN1472 family. It is a TI signal-improvement (SIC) CAN FD transceiver released in June 2024. Figures from TCAN1472-Q1 SLLSFW8A (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tcan1472-q1.pdf, read 2026-09-29T00:38:20Z). Pinout: TXD 1, GND 2, VCC 3, RXD 4, VIO 5 (V variant), CANL 6, CANH 7, STB 8 with an integrated pull-up. The datasheet calls it pin-compatible with the TCAN1044A-Q1 and TCAN1042-Q1. Table 7-4: STB high is standby with the driver disabled, so the enable node drives STB through an inverter, as P2's ranks 1 to 3 do (V18). tMODE, normal to standby or standby to normal: 30 us max (V19: 5 ms). VBUS -58 to +58 V (V24: +30 V). Classic CAN and CAN FD up to 8 Mbps (V21). tPROP(LOOP1) 155 ns max and tPROP(LOOP2) 160 ns max at VIO 3 to 3.6 V (limit 237 ns, margin 77 ns; rank 2 TCAN1044VDRQ1 has 27 ns). VIO 1.7 to 5.5 V, so RXD is at 3.3 V. ILKG_STB(OFF) is -1 to 1 uA at STB = 5.5 V with VCC = VIO = 0 V, so STB has I_off. VCC 4.5 to 5.5 V from the 5 V rail, whose tolerance is open (V100). TJ -40 to 150 degC; the orderable addendum lists TCAN1472VDRQ1 as Active, -40 to 150 degC. Not isolated (V23). On the SOIC-8 footprint it is a rule-5 alternate for P2's ranks 2 and 3 (TCAN1044VDRQ1, TCAN1042HGVDRQ1) in the same circuit. missed.maker: Microchip Technology (JLCPCB API 'Microchip Tech'); S1 Microchip
missed.why: P2 considered the ATA6561 but not the ATA6562/3 family, which adds ISO 11898-2:2016 wake-up on pattern. Figures from DS20005790E (https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/APID/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/ATA6562.3-Data-Sheet-20005790E.pdf, read 2026-09-29T00:42:10Z). SOIC-8 pins: TXD 1, GND 2, VCC 3, RXD 4, VIO 5, CANL 6, CANH 7, STBY 8. That pin set matches the ATA6561 as P2 describes it; the two parts are not compared further. A rising edge on STBY selects standby, so the enable node drives it through an inverter (V18). tdel(norm-stby) 5 us max (V19). DC voltage at CANH and CANL -27 to +42 V (V24). Up to 5 Mbps CAN FD (V21). tPD(TXD-RXD) 210 ns max rising and 200 ns max falling at RL = 60 Ohm and CL = 100 pF (limit 237 ns). VIO 2.8 to 5.5 V; VCC 4.5 to 5.5 V from the 5 V rail (V100 open). Grade 1: Tamb -40 to +125 degC. STBY has a 75 to 175 kOhm pull-up to VCC and no unpowered-leakage figure, so it takes the 4.7 kOhm series resistor, as P2's ATA6561 does. Through 4.7 kOhm, the weakest 75 kOhm pull-up to 5.5 V leaves 0.32 V at a driven-low STBY, under VIL 0.3 x 3.3 = 0.99 V. It ranks with the ATA6561, below ranks 1 to 3 that have I_off, and is the cheapest of the Microchip parts. missed.function: Link terminator (the 120 Ohm at the IO board's end: fitted, switchable or external)
missed.part: fitted split terminator: 120 Ohm split into two equal resistors, with the centre tap to ground through a capacitor
missed.maker: none: an arrangement built from round 2 passives
missed.why: P2 weighed fitted, switchable and external, and left the fitted form undivided. Split termination is a fitted variant that the transceiver datasheets name. TCAN3413 SLLSFS8A section 8.2.1.1 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tcan3413.pdf, read 2026-09-29T00:38:18Z) says: 'If filtering and stabilization of the common-mode voltage of the bus is desired then split termination may be used... Split termination improves the electromagnetic emissions behavior of the network'. The two resistors in series still give 120 Ohm across CANH and CANL, and the capacitor blocks DC. The unpowered check therefore still reads about 60 Ohm with both ends fitted (IOBoard.md:176). P2's reason for rejecting the switchable and external forms applies to it as to a plain fitted resistor: it is always on the bus. The resistor and capacitor values are round 2's. Whether the link needs common-mode filtering is not stated in the tree.

exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: Miss 237 ns: 255 ns max at VCC 4.5 to 5.5 V (FU-A1 P2 readings).
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: The drop holds only if the 5 V rail's tolerance is wider than +/-5 %, and that tolerance is open (V100). TJA1462 Rev. 3.0, 12 February 2025 (https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/data-sheet/TJA1462.pdf, read 2026-09-29T00:48:05Z), Table 9, gives two rows. td(TXDL-RXDL) and td(TXDH-RXDH) are 255 ns max over VCC 4.5 to 5.5 V. Under 'VCC = 4.75 V to 5.25 V' the same parameters are 190 ns max, which meets 237 ns with 47 ns to spare. TJA1463 Rev. 3.0 (https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/data-sheet/TJA1463.pdf, read 00:48:51Z) gives the same 255 ns and 190 ns rows. The TJA1462 meets the other external values at any VCC in 4.5 to 5.5 V. STB (pin 8) is active-high standby with a 20 to 80 kOhm pull-up and no I_off, so it takes the 4.7 kOhm resistor from an inverter. With the weakest 20 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V, a driven-low STB sits at 0.63 V, under VIL 0.99 V. tt(moch) 50 us max (V19). VCANH -36 to +40 V (V24). CAN FD up to 8 Mbit/s (V21). VIO 2.95 to 5.5 V (TJA1462A). The loop delay is the only value tied to the rail. P2 ranks other parts on 'the 5 V rail, whose tolerance is open (V100)' instead of dropping them, so this part belongs on that footing, conditional on V100 at +/-5 % or tighter. JLCPCB C3234095 12072, presale 12044, 0.825 USD at 10 (vendors.py jlcpcb, 00:48:32Z). C3233821 6554, presale 6552, 0.9825 USD at 10 (00:48:33Z). NXP https://www.nxp.com/products/TJA1462 shows 'Status - Active' (00:48:52Z). Digi-Key was not read, because the part passes only if V100 holds.

missed_functions.function: CAN controller clock (the crystal, resonator or oscillator each controller takes)
missed_functions.why: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:169 names 'Controller clock' as a requirement row in state 'required'. IOBoard.md:111 says the CAN bit rate is exact to the controller's clock and that R2 states its tolerance. The R2 row requires R2 to state each controller's clock tolerance. P2 carries that tolerance (V26, V27) as a requirement value of the two controllers, but no entry selects the clock part. Every shortlisted controller needs one. The MCP2518FD takes a '40, 20 or 4 MHz Crystal or Ceramic Resonator' or an external clock. Its Table 7-3 bounds the OSC1 input at +/-0.5 % (DS20006027B, https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/OTH/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/External-CAN-FD-Controller-with-SPI-Interface-DS20006027B.pdf, read 2026-09-29T00:47:30Z). The MCP2515 driver in the tree takes a 16 MHz crystal (IOBoard.md:169). R1 selects the RP2354B's 12 MHz crystal as a function of its own, a round 1 part.
